summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for his 15th cycle of maintenance chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate and rituximab. He reported feeling well with stable chronic floaters in his left eye and no new neurological or systemic symptoms. He received the planned chemotherapy with aggressive hydration and urinary alkalinization to prevent renal toxicity, given his history of methotrexate-induced acute tubular necrosis. Leucovorin rescue was initiated as his methotrexate level declined and continued until levels dropped below 0.1 µM. An MRI of the brain showed no evidence of lymphomatous recurrence and stable post-biopsy changes. A transient rise in liver enzymes and bilirubin was noted, possibly due to an interaction with home aspirin, which was held during admission and safely restarted at discharge. He tolerated treatment well, remained neurologically stable, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up scheduled in six months.
